subject: Brightline onboarding: model shortlist + traffic anchors
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Evans <susan.evans@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brightline onboarding: model shortlist + traffic anchors

Hi team — looping you in for the CS -> Ops handoff on Brightline's onboarding. Quick summary up front and asks at the bottom. Susan, adding you so the implementation squad has direct context; we’ll kick off next Tuesday.

Customer ask / context:
- Product: conversational care assistant (symptom triage + follow-ups).
- Typical conversation: user prompt (50–200 tokens) + context of prior 2–4 messages (avg 800 tokens). Occasional long threads with clinical notes up to ~12k tokens.
- Auth/privacy: PHI possible; they require audit logs and 90-day retention default.

Model shortlist (attached spreadsheet for more detail):
- Model A — 13B / 8k context / quantized (recommended default): balanced latency and quality for multi-turn.
- Model B — 7B / 16k context / q4f: prioritized where long clinical notes appear; slightly lower quality but supports larger context.
- Model C — 4B / 4k / fine-tuned on dialog: low-cost fallback for high-throughput short requests.

Traffic anchors & token projections (sample data attached):
- Expected steady-state: 500k tokens/day (generation + prompt).
- Ramp (first 90 days): 500k -> 1.2M/day.
- Peak days (marketing tranche): up to 2.1M tokens/day.
- Request size distribution: median request -> 900 tokens; 95th percentile -> 3,600 tokens; long-tail (0.8%) > 8k tokens.

Operational considerations / suggested defaults:
- Default rollout: Model A for web/chat flows; route requests with >8k prompt tokens to Model B variant.
- Prefix/KV caching: enable for repeat templated prompts (expected ~18% cache hit).
- Batching: target 8–16ms scheduling window for chat to keep p95 latency < 350ms for Model A.
- Fallback: Model C for cost-sensitive routes (inference budget monitor).

Asks:
1) Grace/Dylan: can you confirm fleet sizing based on the attached sample_traffic_7days.json and recommend a dedicated v-pool vs shared burst plan? Include expected GPU counts for 99th percentile day.
2) Monica: can you draft the rollout plan (canary %s, fallback triggers, monitoring alerts) and a short runbook for switching to Model C under cost pressure?
3) Ops: confirm that audit logs and retention settings can meet 90-day requirement; if not, list changes and timeline.

I'll host a 30-minute kickoff on Tue 08/31 to walk through the spreadsheet and traffic sample — proposed 10:00 PT. Susan, does that time work?

Thanks —
Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: brightline_model_shortlist.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample_traffic_7days.json (json sample)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Evans <susan.evans@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline onboarding: model shortlist + traffic anchors

Thanks Marissa — quick read-through and a few clarifying notes from infra/serving side.

Notes:
- Model choices look sensible. I agree with Model A as the default. For the >8k routing to Model B we should gate by both prompt length and a model-quality signal (e.g., presence of clinical note keyword) so we avoid unnecessary long-context runs.
- Batching: with the projected median/95th we should be able to use continuous batching and keep token-cost low. I'll run a simulation (today) with the sample traffic and send expected GPU-hour estimates.
- Prefix/KV caching: estimate ~15–20% effective cost saving if we cache repeated user session prefixes. We should highlight to Brightline that session affinity improves cache hit.

Immediate asks back to you folks:
- Marissa: can we get the HubSpot contact + expected conversion/activation KPIs so we can tie autoscaling triggers to real business events?
- Dylan: please check quantization profiles for Model B — if q4f yields unacceptable accuracy, we may need to reserve some float16 capacity for high-precision routing.

Rollout suggestion (internal):
- 0–3 days after kickoff: canary at 3% traffic (Model A); monitor p95 latency, error rate, quality regressions against baseline prompts.
- 4–14 days: 20% -> 50% ramp if no regressions; enable routing for >8k detection to Model B for a 5% subset to verify long-context correctness.
- If cost per 1k tokens goes above X threshold (TBD by Dylan), activate Model C for non-critical flows.

I'll attach the simulation numbers to this thread later today.

—Grace
Sr. PM, Serving & Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Susan Evans <susan.evans@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightline ProdOps <prodops@brightlinehealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 10:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline onboarding: model shortlist + traffic anchors

Hi Marissa / team — thanks for the clear summary. 10:00 PT on Tuesday works for our group. A couple of clarifications from Brightline: 

- Compliance: we need role-based access to logs, and a CSV audit export for security reviews. 90-day retention is fine for now; please confirm how redaction works for PHI in logs.
- Traffic: our product analytics folks expect ~120k user interactions/day at launch week (translate to ~1.1M tokens/day with current prompt sizes). Peak concurrency estimate: 420 concurrent chat sessions during promo spikes.
- Long-context fraction: about 0.5% of sessions include long clinical notes that will require >8k context. Those are high-priority and must not be routed to a degraded model.

For the kickoff, we'll bring our SOC/compliance lead and a product engineer to validate retention and access. Also request that you include a quick demo of the fallback/rollout process (how you push a failover to Model C) during the meeting.

Best,
Susan
Head of Product Operations
Brightline Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Evans <susan.evans@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline onboarding: model shortlist + traffic anchors

Thanks all — summarizing next steps and owners before the kickoff: 

Action items:
- Grace: run the serving simulation and share GPU-hour / p95 latency estimates by EOD Tue (owner: grace_oconnor).
- Dylan: validate quantization profiles for Model B and produce a short note on quality tradeoffs (owner: dylan_brooks).
- Marissa: confirm HubSpot contact + activation KPIs and share customer kickoff invite (owner: marissa_cole).
- Monica (me): draft the rollout runbook and a short incident playbook for model fallback; share as a Google Doc before the meeting.
- Ops/Infra: pre-approve audit log retention settings (90d) and RBAC export capability; if anything blocks compliance lead, escalate to security.

Meeting: Tue 2026-09-07 10:00 PT — calendar invite to follow.

I'll attach the draft runbook link after the doc is created. Thank you — concise asks.

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
